## Facts and statements

- [statement] Within its firm-performance reporting scope, the GIPS handbook requires returns after transaction costs and permits estimated transaction costs only for portfolios whose actual transaction costs are not known. (low confidence) — https://www.gipsstandards.org/standards/gips-standards-for-firms/gips-standards-handbook-for-firms/ · keywords: Crypto bot performance and drift uncertainty contracts
- [statement] Evidently’s cited drift documentation requires nonempty reference/current columns and filters empty or infinite values for distribution drift. It says default drift tests do not react to increasing empty counts and recommends separate null-share tests. (low confidence) — https://docs.evidentlyai.com/metrics/explainer_drift · keywords: Crypto bot performance and drift uncertainty contracts

## Proposed guidance — Crypto bot performance and drift uncertainty contracts

PROPOSED: If designing performance/drift reporting, declare portfolio/funding boundary, reserves, return algorithm, denominator, linking, flow timing and valuation provenance. Label fills, costs/funding and marks observed, estimated, unavailable or inapplicable; withhold complete-current-net labels for incomplete evidence and never default missing costs to zero. Match input/decision events, clocks, model/training/configuration/build identity and initial account state across comparison arms. Compare prediction differences and action disagreement on matched events; compare execution on common recorded decisions and model changes on fixed inputs under declared execution assumptions. Display signed costs, funding, inventory and external flows separately; preserve interactions and unallocated residuals instead of claiming causality or alpha. Report windows, raw/usable counts, missingness, estimator/test, score meaning, thresholds, null/dependence assumptions and uncertainty. Require method-specific short-sample/resampling justification; withhold unsupported strong conclusions. Report missing/non-finite counts separately from distribution scores; do not universalize product defaults or estimator-specific results.
